children: Shares of Prestige Consumer Healthcare slid after the company reported a lower second-quarter profit and cut its outlook for the full fiscal year, citing variability in production of its Clear Eyes eye drops.
Shares were down 16% to $44.94 as of midday Thursday, and earlier were on pace for their largest one-day decline since 2010. The stock has fallen 27% this year.

The company said it now expects revenue for the current fiscal year of $1.28 billion to $1.29 billion, with organic revenue growth flat. It previously guided for revenue between $1.290 billion and $1.315 billion with 1% to 3% organic revenue growth.

Adjusted earnings are now expected of $4.48 to $4.55 a share for the fiscal year, down from a range of $4.55 to $4.65 a share. The company also lowered its adjusted free cash flow forecast by $5 million to $265 million or more, from $270 million or more.
Analysts polled by FactSet currently expect revenue of $1.3 billion and adjusted earnings of $4.57 a share.

The outlook change was driven by variability in the production of the company's Clear Eyes drops at Pillar5, which will weigh on revenue in the second half of the fiscal year, Chief Executive Ron Lombardi said.

"It's important to note that our outlook for the remainder of the portfolio is unchanged, with the base business delivering growth and our recent acquisitions on track to deliver sales and profit consistent with our prior guidance," Lombardi said. "Against a challenging consumer environment, this is a testament to our trusted brands and diversified business model."
In the fiscal second quarter, the company's profit came in at $25.3 million, or 53 cents a share. That compares with a profit of $42.2 million, or 86 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were $1.13 a share. Analysts were expecting $1.07 a share.
Revenue grew to $336.3 million, up from $274.1 million a year prior and ahead of expectations for $329.1 million.
